If P(A)=0.8P(A) = 0.8P(A)=0.8, P(B)=0.5P(B) = 0.5P(B)=0.5 and P(B∣A)=0.4P(B|A) = 0.4P(B∣A)=0.4, then P(A∩B)P(A \cap B)P(A∩B) is:

Formula / idea Multiplication rule: P(A∩B)=P(A) P(B∣A)P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B|A)P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B∣A).

  1. 1

    Write the multiplication rule of probability.

    P(A∩B)=P(A)⋅P(B∣A)P(A \cap B) = P(A)\cdot P(B|A)P(A∩B)=P(A)⋅P(B∣A)

Question 2 of 20, Level 1

2MCQ1 mark
The probability that a particular item is available in three shops A, B and C is 45\dfrac{4}{5}54​, 34\dfrac{3}{4}43​ and 23\dfrac{2}{3}32​ respectively. If a person visits all three shops, the probability that the item is available in at least one of them is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea P(at least one)=1−P(none)P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - P(\text{none})P(at least one)=1−P(none), for independent events.

  1. 1

    Find the probability that the item is NOT available in each shop.

    P(A′)=15,P(B′)=14,P(C′)=13P(A') = \dfrac{1}{5},\quad P(B') = \dfrac{1}{4},\quad P(C') = \dfrac{1}{3}P(A′)=51​,P(B′)=41​,P(C′)=31​P(A′)=15,P(B′)=14,P(C′)=13\displaystyle P(A') = \dfrac{1}{5},\quad P(B') = \dfrac{1}{4},\quad P(C') = \dfrac{1}{3}P(A′)=51​,P(B′)=41​,P(C′)=31​
  2. 2

    Shops are independent, so multiply to get 'available in none'.

    P(none)=15⋅14⋅13=160P(\text{none}) = \dfrac{1}{5}\cdot\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{60}P(none)=51​⋅41​⋅31​=601​P(none)=15⋅14⋅13=160\displaystyle P(\text{none}) = \dfrac{1}{5}\cdot\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{60}P(none)=51​⋅41​⋅31​=601​
  3. 3

    Subtract from 1.

    P(at least one)=1−160=5960P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{60} = \dfrac{59}{60}P(at least one)=1−601​=6059​P(at least one)=1−160=5960\displaystyle P(\text{at least one}) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{60} = \dfrac{59}{60}P(at least one)=1−601​=6059​
    1
  4. 4

    Pick the matching option.

    Option (A)\text{Option (A)}Option (A)
Answer(A) 5960\displaystyle \dfrac{59}{60}6059​

Watch out Multiplying the three given probabilities: that is 'available in all three', not 'at least one'.

6Assertion-Reason1 mark
Assertion (A): Events AAA and BBB with P(A)=12P(A) = \dfrac{1}{2}P(A)=21​, P(B)=13P(B) = \dfrac{1}{3}P(B)=31​ and P(A∩B)=16P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{1}{6}P(A∩B)=61​ are independent. Reason (R): Two events AAA and BBB are independent if and only if P(A∩B)=P(A) P(B)P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B)P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B).

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea AAA, BBB independent   ⟺  P(A∩B)=P(A) P(B)\iff P(A \cap B) = P(A)\,P(B)⟺P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B).

  1. 1

    Check A: find P(A) P(B)P(A)\,P(B)P(A)P(B).

    P(A) P(B)=12×13=16=P(A∩B)P(A)\,P(B) = \dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{6} = P(A \cap B)P(A)P(B)=21​×31​=61​=P(A∩B)P(A) P(B)=12×13=16=P(A∩B)\displaystyle P(A)\,P(B) = \dfrac{1}{2}\times\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{6} = P(A \cap B)P(A)P(B)=21​×31​=61​=P(A∩B)
  2. 2

    So A and B are independent. Assertion is true.

  3. 3

    Reason is the definition of independent events. Reason is true.

  4. 4

    A is proved exactly by the test stated in R. R explains A.

  5. 5

    Pick the matching option.

    Option (A)\text{Option (A)}Option (A)
    1
Answer(A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Question 5Question 7

Question 7 of 20, Level 1

7Short answer2 marks
Two cards are drawn one after the other without replacement from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. Find the probability that both are kings.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Multiplication theorem: P(E∩F)=P(E) P(F∣E)P(E \cap F) = P(E)\,P(F|E)P(E∩F)=P(E)P(F∣E).

  1. 1

    Let EEE: first card is a king, FFF: second card is a king.

  2. 2

    Write the multiplication theorem.

    P(E∩F)=P(E)⋅P(F∣E)P(E \cap F) = P(E)\cdot P(F|E)P(E∩F)=P(E)⋅P(F∣E)
    ½
  3. 3

    4 kings in 52 cards.

    P(E)=452P(E) = \dfrac{4}{52}P(E)=524​
    ½
  4. 4

    One king removed: 3 kings left in 51 cards.

    P(F∣E)=351P(F|E) = \dfrac{3}{51}P(F∣E)=513​
    ½
  5. 5

    Multiply and simplify.

    P(E∩F)=452×351=122652=1221P(E \cap F) = \dfrac{4}{52}\times\dfrac{3}{51} = \dfrac{12}{2652} = \dfrac{1}{221}P(E∩F)=524​×513​=265212​=2211​P(E∩F)=452×351=122652=1221\displaystyle P(E \cap F) = \dfrac{4}{52}\times\dfrac{3}{51} = \dfrac{12}{2652} = \dfrac{1}{221}P(E∩F)=524​×513​=265212​=2211​
    ½
  6. 6

    Required probability =1221= \dfrac{1}{221}=2211​.

Answer1221\displaystyle \dfrac{1}{221}2211​

Watch out Using 452×452\dfrac{4}{52}\times\dfrac{4}{52}524​×524​: without replacement, the second draw has 3 kings in 51 cards.

8Short answer3 marks
The chances of P, Q and R getting selected as CEO of a company are in the ratio 4:1:24 : 1 : 24:1:2. The probabilities that the company increases its profits under the new CEO P, Q or R are 0.30.30.3, 0.80.80.8 and 0.50.50.5 respectively. If the company increased its profits, find the probability that it is due to the appointment of R as CEO.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Bayes' theorem: P(Ei∣A)=P(Ei)P(A∣Ei)∑P(Ej)P(A∣Ej)P(E_i|A) = \dfrac{P(E_i)P(A|E_i)}{\sum P(E_j)P(A|E_j)}P(Ei​∣A)=∑P(Ej​)P(A∣Ej​)P(Ei​)P(A∣Ei​)​.

  1. 1

    Let E1,E2,E3E_1, E_2, E_3E1​,E2​,E3​: P, Q, R is selected. Let AAA: profits increase.

  2. 2

    Ratio 4:1:24:1:24:1:2, total 777 parts.

    P(E1)=47,P(E2)=17,P(E3)=27P(E_1) = \dfrac{4}{7},\quad P(E_2) = \dfrac{1}{7},\quad P(E_3) = \dfrac{2}{7}P(E1​)=74​,P(E2​)=71​,P(E3​)=72​P(E1)=47,P(E2)=17,P(E3)=27\displaystyle P(E_1) = \dfrac{4}{7},\quad P(E_2) = \dfrac{1}{7},\quad P(E_3) = \dfrac{2}{7}P(E1​)=74​,P(E2​)=71​,P(E3​)=72​
    1
  3. 3

    Write the given conditional probabilities.

    P(A∣E1)=0.3,P(A∣E2)=0.8,P(A∣E3)=0.5P(A|E_1) = 0.3,\quad P(A|E_2) = 0.8,\quad P(A|E_3) = 0.5P(A∣E1​)=0.3,P(A∣E2​)=0.8,P(A∣E3​)=0.5P(A∣E1)=0.3,P(A∣E2)=0.8,P(A∣E3)=0.5\displaystyle P(A|E_1) = 0.3,\quad P(A|E_2) = 0.8,\quad P(A|E_3) = 0.5P(A∣E1​)=0.3,P(A∣E2​)=0.8,P(A∣E3​)=0.5
    ½
  4. 4

    Find P(A)P(A)P(A) by the theorem of total probability.

    P(A)=47(0.3)+17(0.8)+27(0.5)=1.2+0.8+1.07=37\begin{aligned} P(A) &= \dfrac{4}{7}(0.3) + \dfrac{1}{7}(0.8) + \dfrac{2}{7}(0.5) \\ &= \dfrac{1.2 + 0.8 + 1.0}{7} = \dfrac{3}{7} \end{aligned}P(A)​=74​(0.3)+71​(0.8)+72​(0.5)=71.2+0.8+1.0​=73​​
    ½
  5. 5

    Apply Bayes' theorem for E3E_3E3​.

    P(E3∣A)=P(E3) P(A∣E3)P(A)=27(0.5)37P(E_3|A) = \dfrac{P(E_3)\,P(A|E_3)}{P(A)} = \dfrac{\frac{2}{7}(0.5)}{\frac{3}{7}}P(E3​∣A)=P(A)P(E3​)P(A∣E3​)​=73​72​(0.5)​P(E3∣A)=P(E3) P(A∣E3)P(A)=27(0.5)37\displaystyle P(E_3|A) = \dfrac{P(E_3)\,P(A|E_3)}{P(A)} = \dfrac{\frac{2}{7}(0.5)}{\frac{3}{7}}P(E3​∣A)=P(A)P(E3​)P(A∣E3​)​=73​72​(0.5)​
    ½
  6. 6

    Simplify.

    P(E3∣A)=1/73/7=13P(E_3|A) = \dfrac{1/7}{3/7} = \dfrac{1}{3}P(E3​∣A)=3/71/7​=31​P(E3∣A)=1/73/7=13\displaystyle P(E_3|A) = \dfrac{1/7}{3/7} = \dfrac{1}{3}P(E3​∣A)=3/71/7​=31​
    ½
  7. 7

    Required probability =13= \dfrac{1}{3}=31​.

AnswerP(E3∣A)=13\displaystyle P(E_3|A) = \dfrac{1}{3}P(E3​∣A)=31​

Watch out Answering P(A∣E3)=0.5P(A|E_3) = 0.5P(A∣E3​)=0.5: the question asks for P(E3∣A)P(E_3|A)P(E3​∣A), the reverse direction.

    ½
  6. 6

    Simplify.

    P=2+16=12P = \dfrac{2 + 1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}P=62+1​=21​

    Hence (a) 23\dfrac{2}{3}32​, (b) 12\dfrac{1}{2}21​.

Formula / idea Bayes' theorem with two cases: knows (E1E_1E1​) or guesses (E2E_2E2​).

  1. 1

    Let E1E_1E1​: she knows the answer, E2E_2E2​: she guesses, AAA: answer is correct.

  2. 2

    Write the prior probabilities.

    P(E1)=34,P(E2)=1−34=14P(E_1) = \dfrac{3}{4},\quad P(E_2) = 1 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}P(E1​)=43​,P(E2​)=1−43​=41​P(E1)=34,P(E2)=1−34=14\displaystyle P(E_1) = \dfrac{3}{4},\quad P(E_2) = 1 - \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}P(E1​)=43​,P(E2​)=1−43​=41​

  3. 3

    If she knows, she is surely correct; a guess is right 1 time in 4.

    Apply Bayes' theorem.

    P(E1∣A)=P(E1)P(A∣E1)P(E1)P(A∣E1)+P(E2)P(A∣E2)=34⋅134⋅1+14⋅14P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{P(E_1)P(A|E_1)}{P(E_1)P(A|E_1) + P(E_2)P(A|E_2)} = \dfrac{\frac{3}{4}\cdot 1}{\frac{3}{4}\cdot 1 + \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{1}{4}}P(E1​∣A)=P(E1​)P(A∣E1​)+P(E2​)P(A∣E2​)P(E1​)P(A∣E1​)​=43​⋅1+41​⋅41​43​⋅1​P(E1∣A)=P(E1)P(A∣E1)P(E1)P(A∣E1)+P(E2)P(A∣E2)=34⋅134⋅1+14⋅14\displaystyle P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{P(E_1)P(A|E_1)}{P(E_1)P(A|E_1) + P(E_2)P(A|E_2)} = \dfrac{\frac{3}{4}\cdot 1}{\frac{3}{4}\cdot 1 + \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{1}{4}}P(E1​∣A)=P(E1​)P(A∣E1​)+P(E2​)P(A∣E2​)P(E1​)P(A∣E1​)​=43​⋅1+41​⋅41​43​⋅1​

Formula / idea ∑pi=1\sum p_i = 1∑pi​=1, and every pi≥0p_i \geq 0pi​≥0.

    0+k+2k+2k+3k+k2+2k2+7k2+k=10 + k + 2k + 2k + 3k + k^2 + 2k^2 + 7k^2 + k = 10+k+2k+2k+3k+k2+2k2+7k2+k=10+k+2k+2k+3k+k2+2k2+7k2+k=1\displaystyle 0 + k + 2k + 2k + 3k + k^2 + 2k^2 + 7k^2 + k = 10+k+2k+2k+3k+k2+2k2+7k2+k=1

    10k2+9k−1=010k^2 + 9k - 1 = 010k2+9k−1=0

  3. 3

    (10k−1)(k+1)=0  ⇒  k=110 or k=−1(10k - 1)(k + 1) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; k = \dfrac{1}{10} \text{ or } k = -1(10k−1)(k+1)=0⇒k=101​ or k=−1(10k−1)(k+1)=0  ⇒  k=110 or k=−1\displaystyle (10k - 1)(k + 1) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; k = \dfrac{1}{10} \text{ or } k = -1(10k−1)(k+1)=0⇒k=101​ or k=−1

    Reject k=−1k = -1k=−1, since a probability cannot be negative.

    k=110k = \dfrac{1}{10}k=101​

    Find P(X<3)P(X < 3)P(X<3).

    P(X<3)=P(0)+P(1)+P(2)=0+k+2k=3k=310P(X < 3) = P(0) + P(1) + P(2) = 0 + k + 2k = 3k = \dfrac{3}{10}P(X<3)=P(0)+P(1)+P(2)=0+k+2k=3k=103​P(X<3)=P(0)+P(1)+P(2)=0+k+2k=3k=310\displaystyle P(X < 3) = P(0) + P(1) + P(2) = 0 + k + 2k = 3k = \dfrac{3}{10}P(X<3)=P(0)+P(1)+P(2)=0+k+2k=3k=103​

A laboratory blood test is 99%99\%99% effective in detecting a disease when it is present, but gives a false positive for 0.5%0.5\%0.5% of healthy persons. If 0.1%0.1\%0.1% of the population has the disease, find the probability that a person who tests positive actually has the disease.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

    1
  2. 2

    1
  3. 3

    Write the probabilities of a positive test.

    P(A∣E1)=99%=0.99,P(A∣E2)=0.5%=0.005P(A|E_1) = 99\% = 0.99,\quad P(A|E_2) = 0.5\% = 0.005P(A∣E1​)=99%=0.99,P(A∣E2​)=0.5%=0.005P(A∣E1)=99%=0.99,P(A∣E2)=0.5%=0.005\displaystyle P(A|E_1) = 99\% = 0.99,\quad P(A|E_2) = 0.5\% = 0.005P(A∣E1​)=99%=0.99,P(A∣E2​)=0.5%=0.005

  5. 5

    Substitute the values.
